Senses.Explanation: Heaven and earth hang apart. Chushi Fanqi doubles the saying in one breath — with a hair's difference heaven and earth hang apart, and without a hair's difference heaven and earth still hang apart — then adds that even understanding it is only poking one's head out of a toad's den; Liangting Jingting sets it against the moment of the unthinkable, where one phrase-topic covers all coming deceit; Tianru Weize reads it at the fault-line of one buddha-nature and one wondrous function, where defiled habit alone splits them; and Linji Yixuan, in the sermon Dahui's anthology keeps, brands seeking the meaning through words and letters as far from the dharma as heaven from earth. Gaofeng Yuanmiao grants Yunmen and Yuanwu the crown-eye yet rules their wellsprings worlds apart, Hanyue Fazang says the affair from above is not gotten from another and that cutting off the left arm itself leaves heaven and earth hanging apart, Konggu Daocheng answers a monk's flourished sleeve with the bare doubled saying, Gulin Qingmao answers an inaugural exchange with it in four graphs, Zhongfeng Mingben stamps it into his verse — a hair astray, heaven and earth apart — and mocks glossators who squat in clarity, and Jizong Che rules of two departed worthies that to call them the same leaves heaven and earth hanging apart while to call them different loses the question of coming and going.
